topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the students, outlines the structure and perspectives of the cancer biology lecture series, and introduces the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a disease of genetic changes and differentiation failure
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer arises from accumulated genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal cellular differentiation, tissue architecture, and regulatory multicellular behavior.

topics.label: Distinguishing and classifying benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the biological, histological, and terminological criteria used to distinguish benign from malignant tumors and trace their stepwise invasive progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the physical, functional, and systemic mechanisms by which primary tumors and distant metastases produce disease symptoms and cause death.

topics.label: Cancer incidence in humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the frequency, tissue distribution, and mortality of various tumors across human populations and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical practice of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale, diagnostic methods, and comparative efficacy of population screening programs designed to detect pre-malignant and early-stage tumors.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by referencing the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping details for subsequent practicals and lectures.
